sanskrit_verse: परहस्ताद् गृहीतं यत् कुषीदविधिना ऋणम् । येन यत्र यथा देयम् अदेयं चोच्यते ’धुना ॥
transliteration: parahastād gṛhītaṃ yat kuṣīdavidhinā ṛṇam / yena yatra yathā deyam adeyaṃ cocyate 'dhunā //
sph_interpretive_translation: That debt which has been taken from another's hand without proper method or in neglectful manner must be returned according to the capacity, place, and time of the one who is to give it; and that which is not fit to be given is now declared as such.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the integrity of transactional dharma
Causation follows the conscious capacity of the giver
Restoration logic aligns with sequential dharmic flow
Consciousness alignment governs the fitness of exchange
executable_legal_axioms: IF a debt was acquired through improper means THEN it SHALL be returned based on the current capacity of the debtor
IF an item or value is unfit for transfer THEN it MUST NOT be enforced as legally exchangeable
RESTITUTION shall occur WHERE and WHEN the giver has regained sufficient capacity
NO transaction shall proceed IF it violates the consciousness-state of either party
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating financial restitution or recovery claims, the Supreme Court shall assess not merely legal possession but the dharmic validity of acquisition. Restitution orders must reflect the actual capacity of the obligor at the time of execution, ensuring no artificial burden disrupts their svadharma. The fitness of repayment must align with pramāṇa-based evidence of sustainable capability.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse establishes pramāṇa-based causality by linking obligation to actual capacity rather than abstract liability. It reflects anupūrvaśaḥ by sequencing repayment with the natural restoration of ability. Responsibility is proportional to conscious participation in the act. There is no punitive intent—only alignment with the sequential unfolding of dharmic capacity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process upon verification of original improper receipt
Assess current capacity of debtor through svadharma-aligned metrics
Establish phased return protocol synchronized with debtor's rehabilitative progress
Reintegrate creditor-debtor relationship through meditative acknowledgment of error
Ensure no external pressure disrupts internal dharmic recalibration
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores balance through capacity-conscious restitution, upholds reality as non-punitive, and affirms consciousness as the supreme adjudicator.
